_comment: Per-role write permissions. This file is the enforced permission model:
`agentctl guard check` runs it against every agent-authored diff in CI,
so a worker that ignores its prompt still cannot land an out-of-scope
change. A task spec's allowed_paths NARROWS a role; it never widens one.
dotfiles are in agentlib.guard.ALWAYS_FORBIDDEN and cannot be granted here
`deny` is an explicit belt-and-braces denial checked before `write`.
`write` is an allowlist: a path matching nothing in it is refused.

director._role: Human-driven architecture session. Not dispatched by CI and not subject to this file; its changes land as an ordinary human-reviewed PR from a non-agent branch. Listed here so the model is complete.

manager._role: Decides strategy for one task. Reads; does not commit code.

test_agent._role: Writes the failing tests that define the task's contract.

code_agent._role: Implements until the committed tests pass.

distiller._role: Summarises a CI failure from text handed to it in its prompt. Has no repository access at all - see .ai/docs/threat-model.md.

context_maintainer._role: After a green run, records what changed in the one module file the task named. Commits onto the same task branch so the wiki edit lands in the same human-reviewed PR as the code.

_openapi_json_note: backend/openapi.json is the committed frontend/backend contract: the code
agent regenerates it with backend/scripts/export_openapi.py, and CI fails
the build on any drift. It is granted as one exact path rather than a tree,
because a backend route change that does not refresh it silently breaks the
generated TypeScript client - and the agent that changed the route is the
only one positioned to refresh it.
_dependency_changes: docker-compose.yml are denied to the code agent on purpose: adding a dependency
is a supply-chain decision and a Director call, not something a retry loop makes
on attempt 3 to get a test green.
